key_insight: DynaWeb uses a learned world model of the web to let agents train via simulated interactions instead of expensive, risky live-online trials—enabling fast, safe policy learning for web-based LLM agents.
problem_solved: Training autonomous web agents on the live internet is slow, costly, and risky (privacy, breakage, harmful outputs). This work addresses sample inefficiency and safety by replacing most live interactions with imagined rollouts in a learned web environment.
method: Learn a predictive world model of web dynamics from logs and limited online data (states, actions, responses).
Perform imagined rollouts inside the world model to plan and improve policies (Dyna-style integration of model-based rollouts with RL).
Iteratively collect targeted real interactions to update the model and close the sim-to-real gap, improving robustness and safety.
impact: Enables much more efficient, scalable, and safer training of LLM-powered web agents—reducing cost and risk while accelerating iteration for researchers and practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: real web logs → learned world model → simulated web environment → agent training loop (with periodic real-data updates).
Comparison chart: live-online training vs. model-based simulated training (cost, sample efficiency, safety incidents).
Imagined-rollout schematic: tree of imagined trajectories used for planning/policy updates.
Icons: browser (web), robot/agent, brain/model, shield (safety) to summarize benefits at a glance.
paper_title: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
paper_authors: Hang Ding, Peidong Liu, Junqiao Wang, Ziwei Ji, Meng Cao
